cards.title: "Khana khane ke baad" actually matters
cards.body: Food timing on a prescription isn't decoration. Some medicines work better, or are easier on the stomach, depending on when you eat.

cards.title: Before food
cards.body: Usually means a while before a meal. Ask how long, because the gap can differ from one medicine to another.

cards.title: After food
cards.body: Usually means with a meal or soon after. Often used for medicines that can upset an empty stomach.

cards.title: Empty stomach
cards.body: Typically first thing in the morning, before breakfast. Your pharmacist can tell you how long to wait before eating.

cards.title: Chai counts as something
cards.body: For empty-stomach medicines, tea, milk and that one plain biscuit can count as food. Check with the pharmacist what's allowed.

cards.title: When the parchi doesn't say
cards.body: If food timing isn't written, ask at the chemist counter. It takes ten seconds and saves a lot of guessing.

cards.title: Timing is part of the dose
cards.body: Note it on the strip so everyone at home follows the same routine.

takeaway: Before food, after food and empty stomach instructions matter. Ask your pharmacist about the exact timing for each medicine.
share: Send this to the Papa who takes everything with his morning chai.
